prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1114; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just be called the claimant on this, if that's alright.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road in Pasadena, Texas, in the right lane. Traffic was backed up a bit.
Q: What happened next?
A: I felt a hard jolt from behind. The car lurched forward and I hit the brakes, but there wasn't much I could do. My head snapped back and then forward.
Q: Did you exit your vehicle or speak with the other driver?
A: I got out to look at the damage. The other driver said he was looking at his phone and didn't see the light change in time. He seemed apologetic.
Q: Were there any police or witnesses at the scene?
A: An officer came out and took a report. I think a couple of people in the next lane stopped too, but I didn't get their details.
Q: Did you seek medical attention after the accident?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care that same evening. They said I had a neck strain and gave me a muscle relaxer and told me to rest.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?
A: Yes. My neck is stiff, especially in the morning, and turning to check my blind spot when I drive hurts. Some headaches too, but they come and go.
Q: Have you missed any work because of your injuries?
A: I took a couple of days off and I'm doing lighter duties now. My doctor is seeing me again next week.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm trying to get back to normal and I want this handled fairly.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
